title: Glue invertible modules and nonvanishing sections across discrete intersections
statement: Let $Y$ be a reduced scheme [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and $Z_1,\ldots,Z_r\hookrightarrow Y$ closed subschemes [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose underlying sets cover $Y$. Suppose each $Z_i\cap Z_j$ for $i\ne j$ is a discrete topological space. Given invertible $\mathcal O_{Z_i}$-modules $\mathcal M_i$ [def-sc-invertible-module], there exists an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal M$ restricting to each $\mathcal M_i$. If sections $s_i\in\Gamma(Z_i,\mathcal M_i)$ are nonvanishing at every point of $Z_i\cap Z_j$, $\mathcal M$ can be chosen with a global section $s$ restricting to every $s_i$.

proof.text: Set $T=\bigcup_{i\ne j}Z_i\cap Z_j$. Because each pairwise intersection is discrete, $T$ is discrete. Reducedness together with the set-theoretic cover gives the scheme-theoretic cover $X\setminus T=\bigcup_i(Z_i\setminus T)$, and the opens on the right are pairwise disjoint. The restriction identity for sections on such an open is [lem-sc-glue-component-reduced-cover-sections].

For each $t\in T$, discreteness gives an open neighborhood $U_t$ containing no other point of $T$. Shrink it so that every $\mathcal M_i|_{U_t\cap Z_i}$ is free of rank one; for the prescribed-section assertion, shrink further so each $s_i$ is nonvanishing there and choose the frame carrying $s_i$ to $1$. Cover each $Z_i\setminus T$ by opens $U_{ij}$ on which $\mathcal M_i$ is free, and extend these to an open cover of $X$ by the $U_t$ and $U_{ij}$.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NE, proof, construction of U_t and U_{ij}

proof.text: On overlaps contained in a single $Z_i$, use the transition functions of $\mathcal M_i$. Distinct $U_{ij}$ and $U_{i'j'}$ with $i\ne i'$ are disjoint; on overlaps involving a $U_t$ use the frame chosen on $U_t\cap Z_i$. The restriction identity from step 1 identifies these functions with units on the corresponding overlaps in $X$, and the transition functions satisfy the cocycle condition because they come from the local frames of $\mathcal M_i$. The resulting Cech data glue to an invertible module $\mathcal M$ by [lem-sc-glue-component-transition-cocycle], and its restriction to each $Z_i$ is $\mathcal M_i$.

In the section-prescribed case, the frame on every $U_t$ sends each $s_i$ to $1$. Taking the section $1$ on every $U_t$ and the local expression of $s_i$ on each $U_{ij}$ gives compatible local sections: on overlaps the transition functions are exactly the changes of frames, and on intersections with $U_t$ the normalization makes both expressions equal. The sheaf axiom therefore glues them to a global section $s$ of $\mathcal M$, whose restriction to $Z_i$ is $s_i$.
